assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Atul Ltd (consolidated, ₹ crore). Segment-driven: Life Science Chemicals, Performance & Other Chemicals and Others each grow gross revenue and earn an EBITDA margin (segment EBIT + segment depreciation); a fourth line removes inter-segment sales. Group EBITDA = sum of segments less 'unallocated' (segment results include part of other income; Screener EBITDA excludes it). Valued on P/E, as the street does.

segments.name: Life Science Chemicals
segments._why: FY27: Q1 +4% (₹469 cr); crop-protection exports and APIs grow modestly, domestic agchem hit by weather in FY26; we assume +6% for the year. FY28-29 +8%: new herbicides (MCPP-p and MCPA plant approved Jul-2026, 67 weeks to build, so from FY28), retail launches (three products in May-2026), API ramp-up at Atul Bioscience. LSC grew at only a ~4% CAGR over FY19-26.
segments._revWhy: Driver is gross segment revenue (inter-segment sales are negligible in LSC).
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 19.3% (FY19), 21.0%, 21.3%, 15.3%, 24.0%, 18.4%, 24.3%, 26.9% (FY26, the best in eight years). Q1FY27 EBIT margin 19.8% (~23.5% EBITDA). 2,4-D and other actives face Chinese pricing; we use 24.5%, about the FY23-26 average, not the FY26 peak.

segments.name: Performance & Other Chemicals
segments._why: FY27: Q1 ₹1,427 cr (+34%) on war-time chemical prices and volume; we assume ~₹1,250 cr a quarter for Q2-Q4 as prices normalise: +12%. FY28 +8%, FY29 +9%: volume growth from the 50 ktpa liquid epoxy resin expansion (Oct-2024), Atul Products' caustic-chlorine chain and debottlenecking, with flat prices. FY19-26 CAGR was 7%.
segments._revWhy: Driver is gross segment revenue, including ~₹220 cr a year of inter-segment sales (removed in the eliminations line).
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 18.9% (FY19), 23.1%, 26.1% (FY21 peak), 18.6%, 10.3% (FY23 trough), 12.0%, 14.4%, 14.3% (FY26). Q1FY27 EBIT margin 16.8% (~21% EBITDA) included inventory gains and war-time spreads (ICICI Securities: unlikely to sustain). FY27 17% (Q1 ~21%, then ~15.5%); FY28 15.5% and FY29 16%: modest improvement on FY26 from LER utilisation, the Indian anti-dumping duty on epoxy resin (Nov-2025) and China's capacity discipline, still well below FY19-22.

segments.name: Others (agri-biotech, services)
segments._why: Tissue-culture date palms (DPD UK, Atul Rajasthan Date Palms) and services: ₹80 cr in FY26 (+9%); we assume +10% a year.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin 22-24% in FY25-26 (EBIT + depreciation); 20% assumed.

segments.name: Inter-segment eliminations
segments._why: Sales between segments (almost all from P&OC: caustic, chlorine, intermediates), removed on consolidation: ₹240 cr (FY25), ₹221 cr (FY26), ₹75 cr in Q1FY27 alone. We assume ~₹260 cr in FY27, then growth in line with P&OC.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Segment EBITDA above reported EBITDA (other income allocated to segments, less central costs)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA (which excludes other income): ₹45 cr (FY19), ₹64 cr, ₹40 cr, ₹39 cr, ₹51 cr, ₹48 cr, ₹97 cr (FY25), ₹128 cr (FY26, incl. exchange gains). Q1FY27 ~₹22 cr. We assume ₹100-105 cr.
assumptions._capexWhy: Capex has been cut from ₹875 cr (FY23) and ₹504 cr (FY24) to ₹270 cr (FY25) and ₹175 cr (FY26) as the company 'conserves cash'. FY27: the ₹167 cr MCPP-p/MCPA plant (67 weeks), debottlenecking, renewable power and maintenance; FY28-29 rising as management 'evaluates large investments' (Nuvama, May-2026). No large project has been announced; any big one would be upside to capex and, later, revenue.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹322 cr = 7.5% of average gross block (₹4,274 cr); Q1FY27 ₹78 cr. 7.3% gives ~₹327 / ₹350 / ₹377 cr as new plants are added.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Treasury book (cash + current investments + equity stakes, less borrowings) ~₹2,500 cr at Mar-26 in the model. FY26 treasury income: dividends ₹20 cr, interest ₹21 cr (incl. a one-off tax-refund interest), fair-value and sale gains on treasury funds ₹77 cr. 4.75% on the opening book, plus ₹20 cr of other non-operating income.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Lease income, insurance claims, miscellaneous items (₹19-28 cr a year), excluding exchange gains (₹44 cr in FY26) which we do not forecast.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹17 cr; Q1FY27 ₹4 cr. Term loans of ₹173 cr in Atul Products amortise.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective 23.5% (tax refunds); Q1FY27 26.8%; statutory 25.17% plus disallowances.
assumptions._payoutWhy: ₹30 dividend on FY26 (15% standalone payout, 13% of consolidated EPS); buybacks (₹50 cr FY21, ₹70 cr FY23, ₹50 cr FY24) are not modelled.

dcf._betaWhy: Diversified chemicals with a net-cash balance sheet and no leverage: slightly below market risk (Ke 11.9%).
dcf._tgWhy: Indian chemical demand grows with nominal GDP; 5.5% for ever.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~9% in FY29 to 8% by FY37: volume-led growth on existing sites and new projects.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin drifts to 18%: the FY19-26 average was ~19% on Screener's basis; FY26 16.5%.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex rises to 5% of revenue (FY19-26 average ~8%, FY25-26 ~3-4%) to fund growth.
dcf._yearsWhy: Ten-year explicit-plus-fade period; the business needs no long project horizon.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Chinese capacity discipline and India's anti-dumping duties keep P&OC margins near Q1FY27 levels (~19%); the epoxy and caustic-chlorine plants run full; crop protection recovers with exports; a large new project is announced and funded from cash.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: War-time spreads unwind fully and Chinese dumping returns: P&OC margins fall back to the FY23-24 trough (~12-13%); 2,4-D prices fall and LSC margins return to ~21%; growth stalls as it did in FY23-24.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Atul: Motilal Oswal 25x and Nuvama 30x FY28E EPS (2026). 21x = the stock's 34.6x one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021, excluding FY24 as a trough year under the house rule (41.1x including it), cut by the ~30% de-rating of Indian chemical stocks at 30-Sep-2026 (≈24x), less ~15% because ROE (~12%) only matches the 11.9% cost of equity (≈20.6x, rounded to 21x). Bull 24x (no returns discount), bear 17x (base less ~20%, the same spread as before; near the stock's FY20 forward-P/E band of 15-22x).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Separates the large net cash from the operating business. 14x ≈ the 24x five-year median EV/EBITDA, less the same ~30% sector de-rating and ~15% returns discount; peers at 30-Sep-2026 traded at 16-20x trailing (Vinati 16.9x, Deepak 16.1x, Aarti 16.0x, PI 18.1x, SRF 19.8x), Atul 12.5x.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: ten-year fade to 8% growth and an 18% EBITDA margin, capex 5% of revenue, Ke 11.9% (beta 0.9), terminal growth 5.5%, Mar-27 net cash added.

cover.headline: Q1 was a spike; on normal earnings this cash-rich chemical house is fairly priced
cover.lead: Atul makes crop-protection actives and pharma ingredients (Life Science Chemicals, ~28% of revenue but 50% of segment profit) and a wide range of performance chemicals: epoxy resins, aromatics, dyes, caustic-chlorine (Performance & Other Chemicals, ~72%). Q1FY27 was its best quarter ever (EPS ₹83, +92%) on war-time chemical prices and inventory gains that we expect to fade, so we model FY28E EPS of only ₹272.0 (+3%), 19% below Motilal Oswal. At ₹5,916 the stock trades at 20.4x Sep-28E EPS and holds ~₹3,100 cr of net cash by Mar-27 (~18% of its market value). We value Atul as the street does, on **P/E: 21x Sep-28E EPS of ₹290.7**, which gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** EV/EBITDA (₹7,743) is higher because it credits the net cash in full; our DCF (₹5,376) is a little lower. Both bracket the price: the good business and the cash are paid for, the Q1 spike is not. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Life Science Chemicals is the jewel
arguments.p: Atul holds 13% of the world market in the herbicide 2,4-D and 14% in the insecticide indoxacarb. LSC earned ₹417 cr of EBIT in FY26 (23.1% margin) on ₹1,805 cr of revenue, a 39.5% pre-tax return on its capital. Growth is slow (~4% a year over FY19-26) and Chinese pricing caps it, but it is a genuinely high-return franchise.

arguments.h: P&OC: big plants, thin returns, now being sweated
arguments.p: Atul spent ₹1,970 cr in FY22-24, mostly in P&OC (an 80 ktpa epoxy resin plant, a 300 TPD caustic-chlorine plant, aromatics). P&OC EBIT fell from ₹576 cr (FY22) to ₹240 cr (FY24) and its ROCE is still only 14.2% (FY26). The plants now run without new capex; India's anti-dumping duty on epoxy imports (Nov-2025) helps. Q1FY27's 16.8% EBIT margin was a war-time spike; we model ~15.5% EBITDA (FY26: 14.3%).

arguments.h: A cash machine with a capital-allocation question
arguments.p: Capex fell from ₹875 cr (FY23) to ₹175 cr (FY26) and free cash flow reached ₹848 cr. Net cash grows to ~₹4,400 cr by FY29E in our model. That pile holds ROE at ~11%, about the cost of equity. Three buybacks returned only ₹170 cr since 2020. Better use of the cash is upside we do not model.

arguments.h: Valuation: fair once the trough year is left out
arguments.p: Brokers use 25-30x FY28E EPS on higher earnings. Atul's one-year-forward P/E median since 2021 is 34.6x leaving out FY24, a trough year under our house rule (41x with it). Indian chemical stocks were ~30% below their medians on 30-Sep-2026 (Atul −46%), so ~24x, less ~15% because returns only match the cost of equity: 21x. The stock is at 21.7x our FY28E: about fair.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): how much of Q1's P&OC margin (16.8% EBIT vs ~9% in FY26) survives as war-time prices and inventory gains fade.
Utilisation of the 80 ktpa epoxy resin plant and Atul Products' caustic-chlorine chain; epoxy exports to the US despite its anti-dumping duty (12.69% for Atul).

The ₹167 cr MCPP-p/MCPA herbicide plant (approved Jul-2026, 67 weeks) and new crop-protection launches.

sections.title: One giant integrated site, two very different businesses

blocks.p: Atul was set up in 1947 by Kasturbhai Lalbhai and started manufacturing at Atul, near Valsad in south Gujarat, in 1952. Today the 1,300-acre site, with its own 73 MW power plant, effluent treatment and basic chemicals (chlorine, caustic soda, sulphuric acid), feeds more than 900 products sold to ~4,000 customers in 88 countries; 40% of FY26 revenue came from outside India. The products fall into two reported segments. **Life Science Chemicals** (LSC) sells crop-protection actives (2,4-D, indoxacarb, sulfonylurea herbicides), branded crop-protection products for Indian farmers and pharmaceutical ingredients. **Performance & Other Chemicals** (P&OC) sells epoxy resins and hardeners, aromatics (para-cresol and its derivatives), dyes and pigments, resorcinol and bulk chemicals, and Lapox/Polygrip adhesives. Key group entities: Atul Products (caustic-chlorine, 100%), Atul Bioscience (APIs, 100%), Amal (49.86%, consolidated), DPD (date palms, UK) and joint ventures with Rudolf (textile chemicals), Nouryon (Anaven, monochloroacetic acid) and Buckman (water treatment).

sections.title: Chemicals: China sets the price; India is protecting its producers

blocks.p: China makes 46% of the world's chemicals (26% in 2010); India makes under 3% and is the world's largest net importer. When Chinese demand slowed in 2023-24, surplus Chinese product cut prices across Atul's markets: epoxy, para-cresol, dyes, 2,4-D. That is why Atul's revenue fell 13% in FY24 and P&OC margins halved. Since late 2025 the picture has improved: China launched an "anti-involution" campaign against loss-making capacity and cut export tax rebates, India imposed anti-dumping duties on epoxy resin (Nov-2025, Atul was an applicant) and sulphur black, and the India-US trade deal (Feb-2026) cut US tariffs on Indian goods to ~18%. Then the West Asia conflict (from Mar-2026) pushed up crude-linked raw material and chemical prices, which inflated Q4FY26-Q1FY27 margins across Indian chemicals. By August, spreads in several chains were already easing.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Atul has a **narrow moat in LSC** (global scale in 2,4-D and indoxacarb, registrations, an integrated chain) and a **cost advantage from its integrated site**, not a moat in P&OC. In epoxy, aromatics and dyes it is a price-taker against Chinese supply: P&OC margins fell from 26% to 10% in two years. What protects shareholders is the balance sheet, not pricing power. A business like this earns 20%+ ROE at the top of the cycle (FY20) and single digits at the bottom (FY24: 6.6%).

sections.title: Ten years, two cycles: a 2020-21 peak, a 2024 trough, a record FY26 and a war-time Q1

blocks.p: Atul's revenue rose from ₹2,637 cr in FY15 to ₹5,428 cr in FY23, fell 13% to ₹4,726 cr in FY24 as crop-protection customers destocked and Chinese suppliers cut prices, then recovered to a record ₹6,274 cr in FY26. Profit followed a deeper cycle: net profit peaked at ₹671 cr (EPS ₹225) in FY20, halved to ₹324 cr (EPS ₹110) in FY24, and only regained the old peak in FY26 (₹689 cr, EPS ₹230), helped by ₹206 cr of other income. In other words, shareholders waited six years for earnings to grow. Q1FY27 then delivered the best quarter in the company's history: revenue +25%, EBITDA margin 21%, EPS ₹83 (+92%).

blocks.p: Over FY17-26 Atul generated ₹5,982 cr of operating cash, spent ₹3,680 cr on plants, paid ₹629 cr of dividends and ₹170 cr on three buybacks, and still added ~₹1,500 cr to its treasury. The first five years were excellent: capex of ₹1,265 cr, ROCE of 19-28%. The next five (FY22-26) were not: ₹2,415 cr of capex, two-thirds of it in FY22-24 for liquid epoxy resin, a caustic-chlorine plant (Atul Products) and API capacity, while ROCE fell to 9% in FY24. Management then braked hard: capex fell to ₹270 cr (FY25) and ₹175 cr (FY26), and free cash flow jumped to ₹848 cr.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean books; strip out other income swings and Q1's inventory gains

bullets: **Other income is large and volatile.** ₹203 cr in FY26 (22% of PBT): fair-value gains on treasury funds ₹77 cr, exchange gains ₹44 cr, interest ₹21 cr (including a one-off tax refund), dividends ₹20 cr, an interest subsidy ₹15.5 cr. We forecast only treasury income at 4.75% plus ₹20 cr of other items (~₹139 cr in FY27E), not exchange gains.

**Segment results include part of other income.** The sum of segment EBITDA exceeded reported EBITDA (excluding other income) by ₹128 cr in FY26 (₹97 cr in FY25, ~₹40-60 cr before). Segment margins therefore look a little better than the group's.
**Q1FY27 had inventory gains.** Inventories fell by ₹188 cr in the quarter as stock bought earlier was sold at war-time prices; ICICI Securities called the spread jump "unlikely to sustain".

**Equity stakes go through OCI.** ~₹870 cr of listed shares (Pfizer ₹453 cr, Arvind ₹140 cr, BASF India ₹84 cr and others) move equity, not profit: total comprehensive income was ₹375 cr in Q1FY27 vs PAT ₹254 cr.
**Minority interest.** Amal (49.86%) is consolidated; ₹11 cr of FY26 profit (₹8.6 cr in Q1FY27) belongs to its other shareholders. Reported EPS is on owners' profit; our model's EPS is equivalent.

**Audit and legal.** Deloitte Haskins & Sells: unmodified opinion, no key audit matters (FY26); contingent liabilities only ~₹11 cr; a GST demand of ₹8.3 cr plus ₹8.4 cr penalty (Dec-2025) is under appeal; ₹152 cr of guarantees for Atul Products' loans.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Conservative books, a Big-4 auditor with no key audit matters, tiny contingent liabilities and no leverage. The adjustments investors should make are about earnings quality, not accounting: ignore exchange gains and fair-value swings in other income, and treat Q1FY27's inventory gains as one-off.

primary.name: P/E
primary.why: How the street values Atul: Motilal Oswal 25x and Nuvama 30x FY28E EPS (2026). 21x = the stock's 34.6x one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021, excluding FY24 as a trough year under the house rule (41.1x including it), cut by the ~30% de-rating of Indian chemical stocks at 30-Sep-2026 (≈24x), less ~15% because ROE (~12%) only matches the 11.9% cost of equity (≈20.6x, rounded to 21x). Bull 24x (no returns discount), bear 17x (base less ~20%, the same spread as before; near the stock's FY20 forward-P/E band of 15-22x).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: War-time spreads unwind fully and Chinese dumping returns: P&OC margins fall back to the FY23-24 trough (~12-13%); 2,4-D prices fall and LSC margins return to ~21%; growth stalls as it did in FY23-24.
